cases.observation: The Samaritan and Old Greek controls preserve an invitation absent from WLC. Direct Hebrew witness 4Q2 instead moves from 'his brother' straight into the field scene, proving that the shorter form was already in circulation in the Judean Desert period. That establishes antiquity, not automatic priority.
cases.english_effect: The current shorter main text remains defensible. Its footnote should now disclose that 4Q2 supports the shorter transition while the Samaritan, Old Greek, and Vulgate traditions preserve the invitation.

cases.observation: The Samaritan control relocates the altar instructions into its extended 26:35 node. Its 30:6-equivalent and Rahlfs 30:6 both lack the extra mercy-seat placement clause in WLC, but Rahlfs retains the block at chapter 30. Agreement on a local clause is therefore not agreement on passage order. The Greek meeting/disclosure wording is not exact Hebrew attestation. No direct Judean Desert attestation of the 30:6 clause is asserted here. 4Q11's published transition at 26:35-36 is discussed separately as order evidence, not evidence for the mercy-seat wording. Shorter-source priority, deliberate expansion and accidental omission remain competing explanations pending full apparatus and manuscript review.
cases.english_effect: Retain WLC and the existing English words. Correct misplaced lexical footnotes, place the atonement-cover note after mercy seat, and disclose the shorter clause and alternate block position in a new textual note. Pre-edit verse hash e3ae69508898dc32cbaae7042d9965c9e518fab213c20f130a38cac27762ecb1. Footnote markers changed, not English wording; no critical-source promotion or full-verse English approval.

cases.observation: 4Q13 preserves seventy-five; 4Q1 preserves 'and five' after reconstructed 'seventy.' The whole numeral in 4Q11 is reconstructed inside brackets, so it supplies no preserved count reading. Its Joseph clause is partly visible after that gap. The count and Joseph clause require separate decisions: 4Q13 proceeds to Joseph's death, while the Old Greek places the location clause before the count. Samaritan and Masoretic controls read seventy. Physical distinctness or script does not establish genealogical independence.
cases.english_effect: The main text remains at seventy pending image verification and formal adjudication, but a textual footnote is now required. A future seventy-five decision would affect the number; a separate decision would govern the Joseph clause and its position. Acts 7:14 is reception evidence and must not be counted as another Hebrew manuscript.

cases.observation: 2Q2 reconstructs the entire geographical phrase and duration in brackets; it supplies no preserved geographical reading. 4Q14 partly preserves Egypt followed directly by the duration, excluding Canaan after Egypt at this location. Its reconstructed beginning cannot exclude Canaan before Egypt or 'their fathers.' The Samaritan adds the fathers and orders Canaan before Egypt; the Rahlfs LXX control lacks the fathers and orders Egypt before Canaan. Neither fragment establishes the full Egypt-only form from preserved letters alone.
cases.english_effect: The current main text remains aligned to its declared Masoretic base without a new priority decision. The note must explain the fragments' limited support rather than claim two Egypt-only witnesses, and must keep the distinct Samaritan and Old Greek forms separate.

cases.observation: The Masoretic and Old Greek controls have Ebal, while the Samaritan control has Gerizim. 4Q33 establishes that this verse was present in a Judean Desert Hebrew manuscript, but the whole mountain-name phrase is editorially supplied inside a lacuna. It cannot vote for either Ebal or Gerizim; unprovenanced or private-market fragments are excluded from this evidence set.
cases.english_effect: The current Ebal main text remains pending rather than newly confirmed. Its note now reports the Samaritan reading and states explicitly that 4Q33 is indeterminate at the decisive word.

cases.observation: Direct Hebrew manuscript 4Q44 preserves a longer form with heavens, all gods, sons, and repayment of those who hate him. The Old Greek preserves a related but still longer form, adding distinct calls to the nations and all angels. The Samaritan and Masoretic controls share the shorter form. The longer witnesses therefore cannot be collapsed into one identical reading.
cases.english_effect: The note now quotes the 4Q44 form accurately and distinguishes it from the still longer Old Greek. A longer English main text is a serious adjudication candidate, but no wording is selected before image verification and full external-and-internal review.

cases.observation: Direct Hebrew witness 4Q37 reads 'sons of God' at the decisive phrase. The Rahlfs Greek control's 'angels of God' supports the same divine referent but not necessarily the identical Hebrew spelling. Amherst 192's published αγγε prefix independently distinguishes the angel noun, not the complete phrase. The Masoretic and Samaritan controls read 'sons of Israel.' Paleo-Hebrew 4Q45 cannot vote on the final phrase. Cambridge p^b(uid), mapped to 106, reports sons of Israel; do not import the contrary secondary complete-phrase attribution as verified sons-of-God support. See discovery/deut32_8_greek_review.v1.json.
cases.english_effect: The existing working adjudication favoring a divine referent is strengthened by a pinned direct-manuscript transcription. 'According to the number of the sons of God' is the leading critical English candidate, while 'angels of God' is a Greek interpretation and 'sons of Israel' remains the current WLC-aligned main text. Canonical promotion still requires an explicit critical-source record and image verification.
